title: gdp-wired interchange format, version 1.0
description: A rule, its laws and a certificate that the laws hold, as JSON any language can read, write and check. A document is one certificate of one kind. The meaning of each kind (which goals it stands for and when it is accepted) is in docs/interchange.md; this schema fixes the shapes. Three rules hold throughout: every record is a list of [name, value] pairs in order (never a JSON object), every number is a safe integer (|n| <= 2^53 - 1) unless said otherwise, and a linear form lists its constant first, then its [coefficient, atom] pairs in the order the kernel built them. A checker for version 1.m reads every 1.n with n <= m and refuses any field it doesn't know.

version.description: The format's version: major.minor. A minor version adds optional fields or kinds; a major one changes a meaning.

kind.description: The certificate's kind: which fields follow and what they claim.

meta.description: Anything the producer keeps beside the certificate (its name and version, the run that made it, a capture's answer). Never read by a checker; kept by a round trip.

columns.description: The term columns: atom {"col": i} in any linear form of this document stands for the value of columns[i], a choice (a truncated subtraction, a min, a max or an if) that the path where it is read leaves open. Columns are named by their terms, so two equal terms are one column. Any order; present only where some atom reads one.

goals.description: Goals over the naturals, each with its tree. Claim: each goal's hypotheses never hold together. Each goal is a claim of its own.
Goals over the rationals, each with its tree (no cut; strict rows). Claim: each goal's hypotheses never hold together over the rationals.

proof.description: Claim: every law holds in every reachable state (by induction: each holds at the start, and one step from a state where all hold keeps it). The laws are proven together, so each is accepted exactly when all are.

stepLaws.description: Claims about what steps do: in every reachable state, every allowed request (k of them in a row, for steps: k) satisfies the step law's then. The laws are proven too and assumed.

laws.description: Laws proven inductive on their own and assumed.

kInduction.description: Claim: the plain law holds in every reachable state, by k-induction: at the start, after every run of j < k steps from the start, and after any k steps in a row each starting where it holds (KInd.lean's kind_sound).

law.description: A plain law: no forall, keys, some or ex.

proof.description: The laws' proof, and a tree for the start goal (<law> @start, its instances in perStep under that name) and for each k-step goal (<law> @base j @j steps, <law> @k-step @k steps).

progress.description: Claim: in every reachable state where when holds, the named request is allowed and the step it causes makes then hold.

then.description: The state before by plain names, after by primed ones (s', M'[k]).

request.description: A term per input, over the state and params: the request named.

instances.description: The keys each every-key law is assumed at in the progress goals.

trees.description: A tree per progress goal: <name>: the request is allowed (where the machine has an assumption) and <name>: the step it causes.

lawsProof.description: The laws' own proof, which the claim assumes. Without it the claim is refused.

proof.description: The proof of the liveness's step laws (stay, cover and one per helpful request, as kernel.ts's livenessParts builds them), with the laws'.

laws.description: Invariants: plain laws over the state and params.

rank.description: A natural over the state and params, or a list of them compared in order (lexicographically), that drops on every turn. Claim: the loop halts from every start (Live.lean's loop_halts_of), and each invariant holds.

trees.description: A tree per goal of kernel.ts's loopObligations.

laws.description: Plain laws over the fold's values and params. Claim: each holds of every tree (at every leaf, and at a node whenever it holds at both children).

holds.description: Over the state and params, no input.

laws.description: Claim: each law holds in every reachable state, the state rationals.

trees.description: Per law: [name, {start, step}], the trees of its start goal and its step goal.

functions.description: The ring of functions (one, or several calling each other) whose termination this is.

text.description: The measures as the producer writes them, for people.

measures.description: A measure per function, in order.

obligations.description: Each call's obligation (the measure drops across it) with its cyclic proof. The kernel checks each proof; that these are the measures' obligations is read from the functions' definitions, which the format does not carry (Lean checks that: Data.lean, termination_by).

name.description: A name: nonempty, not __proto__, and not a canonical array index (0, 7, 42), which a JavaScript object lists before its other keys. A variable read in a linear form also has none of * [ ] , : and is not 1.

nat.description: A natural number within the safe integers.

E.description: A term over the naturals (Lean's Kern.E): every value it computes is a natural.

op.description: a + b; a - b truncated at 0; min; max; a × b (a product: the kernel reads its monomials as atoms).

map.description: A map (or a function of the rule, read like one).

op.description: Of any number of parts (and of none is true, or of none false).

name.description: A flag of the machine's step, read in its terms (never in a goal: flags are inlined first).

keys.description: Further bound keys (a condition at every tuple of keys).

witness.description: Under a not in a law: a term naming the key where the condition fails.

oneOf.description: c at every key: only as a whole flag of the step (a quantified flag) or under a not in a law.

Rat.description: A rational, any size: numerator and denominator in decimal.

QE.description: A term over the rationals (Rationals.lean's Q.E): subtraction not truncated.

QC.description: A condition over the rationals (Q.C): and and or binary.

PairsE.description: A record of terms: [name, term] pairs, in order, each name once.

PairsC.description: A record of conditions: [name, condition] pairs, in order.

PairsNat.description: A record of naturals: [name, natural] pairs, in order.

Lin.description: A linear form Σ cᵢ·aᵢ + c (a row reads it as <= 0). First the constant c, or null when the form has none (a form with constant 0 written is another form: its canonical text differs). Then [cᵢ, aᵢ] pairs, each atom once, in the order the kernel built them: a leaf's rows are found in that order, and a derivation names rows by their place. Coefficients may be 0 where the kernel kept one.

oneOf.description: A map's cell: the map read at a key, itself a linear form. The kernel names it map[canon(key)].
A monomial: the product of two factors or more, each a variable or a cell (no column). Named by its factors' names sorted (by UTF-16 code units) and joined by *.
A term column: the value of the document's columns[col].

Step.description: A derivation's step: each makes a row, numbered from 0 in order.

prefixItems.description: The leaf's i-th row (docs/interchange.md says how a leaf's rows are listed).

oneOf.description: ["input", i]: a row of the leaf.
["combine", a, b, ma, mb]: ma·row a + mb·row b (strict when either is, over the rationals).

prefixItems.description: g > 0, dividing every variable coefficient of the row.

oneOf.description: ["cut", of, g]: the row's coefficients divided by g and its constant rounded up (over the integers only: Cert.lean's cut_sound).

Tree.description: A proof tree: splits on linear atoms, a derivation at each leaf. Accepted when every leaf's derivation refutes its rows.

split.description: The atom split on: yes is split <= 0, no is split >= 1 (over the rationals, -split < 0). Never one the path decides already, never a constant.

leaf.description: The derivation: its last row must have every variable coefficient 0 and a positive constant (or, strict over the rationals, a constant >= 0).

squares.description: Linear forms t whose squares (-t·t <= 0) follow the leaf's rows (naturals only).

products.description: Pairs [i, j] of rows (the leaf's, its squares', earlier products'): p <= 0 and q <= 0 give -p·q <= 0, appended in order (naturals only).

Trees.description: Trees by goal: [goal name, tree] pairs, each name once. A goal's name is the kernel's (<law> @start, <law> @step, <step law> @step law, <step law> @k steps, ...).

hyps.description: The hypotheses, over naturals (every variable >= 0), with no flag.

tree.description: No cut, no product, no square.

Instances.description: For each law that holds at every key (and each quantified flag, as ?<flag>), the keys a proof assumes it at: [law name, terms]. A law about several keys has its tuples flattened, its forall key first.

LawsProof.description: The induction's proof: the instances for each law's goals, and a tree per goal (<law> @start, <law> @step; a history's relation i @record and prune @query q).

instances.description: [law name, Instances]: the instances its two goals use.

StepProof.description: The laws' proof, and the step laws'.

instances.description: The instances every step law's goal uses, unless it has its own.

perStep.description: [step law name, Instances]: a step law's own instances.

trees.description: A tree per step law goal.

MapUpdate.description: A write to a map in a step.

each.description: The bound key, read in value only as a map's key.

History.description: A log of requests the machine keeps (kernel.ts's historyMachine; History.lean).

record.description: The inputs a record keeps, read as r.<input>.

sums.description: State variables worth the sum over the log of a term of the record and params.

queries.description: Inputs worth the sum over the log of a term of the record, params and the request's other inputs.

holds.description: a <= b, homogeneous over sums and queries.

relations.description: Relations proven per record, assumed at every step.

Fn.description: A function the rule reads and never writes, read like a map at any key. The kernel knows it only by the machine's facts; the rest is for the runtimes and the Lean export.

lean.description: A Lean term of type Nat → Nat.

call.description: Its JavaScript on its arguments themselves.

Recurrence.description: A function defined by a recurrence on its first argument (for the Lean export; not read by the kernel).

Machine.description: A step machine: the rule (core/machine.ts's Machine).

state.description: The state variables, in order, each with its start value over the params.

maps.description: The maps, each with the value every cell starts at.

flags.description: Named conditions decided before the step, each reading the flags before it; a quantified flag is an all.

state.description: Each state variable's value after the step (one left out keeps its value).

pre.description: A precondition over the params alone: it holds at the start and at every step.

assume.description: What each request meets: it holds at a step, never at the start.

facts.description: Laws over the params and functions alone, assumed in every goal, never proven here.

Law.description: A law: a condition on the state and params (and maps).

name.description: Unique among the laws and facts; not starting with ?.

holds.description: What is proven (for a law with some, the witnessed body).

forall.description: The key it holds at every value of.

keys.description: Further keys (a law about every two keys or more).

stated.description: The law as written, where holds is the stronger law proven (a key named by a witness).

some.description: The naturals it says exist (never handed to the kernel).

ex.description: What a law with there-exists states: ∃ vars. body.

StepLaw.description: What one step (or k steps in a row) does.

when.description: Narrows the requests: one condition for the first step, or one per step.

then.description: The state, maps, params and first request before by plain names; the state and maps after the last step by primed names (s', M'[k]); the j-th request (j >= 2) as input@j.

Liveness.description: Claim: whenever from holds, to holds later, in every run that takes each helpful request infinitely often (Live.lean's leads_sound, sleads_sound).

rank.description: Naturals over the state and params, compared in order.

request.description: The one helpful request (or helpful, not both).
Some inputs by terms over the state and params; the others free.

Loop.description: A loop: body runs while while holds, each turn reading fresh inputs.

Recur.description: Claim: for some params meeting the precondition, a run of turns from the start never ends (NonTerm.lean's never_ends_of). A closed recurrent set with its successor given.

stem.description: Each turn's inputs from the start into the set (an input not named is 0), evaluated exactly.

wit.description: A term per input over the state and params: the turn taken from the set.

tree.description: Refutes the closure goal: the set, and the witnessed turn failing while or the assumption or leaving the set.

Fold.description: A fold over binary trees whose leaves and nodes carry inputs.

leaf.description: A leaf's values from its inputs.

node.description: A node's values from its children's (l_<name>, r_<name>) and its own inputs; the same names as leaf.

Cyclic.description: A cyclic proof (kernel/cyclic.ts; Cyclic.lean's cyclic_sound): sequents whose uses of each other lower a rank. Claim: each node's hypotheses imply its conclusion wherever the facts hold. No flag, no quantifier anywhere in it.

holds.description: Holds at every value of its keys.

rank.description: Naturals compared in order; every use's node has a rank of the same length.

at.description: Terms for its keys (the shorter list decides).

insts.description: The facts at the terms this node's goals assume them.

main.description: Refutes the node's goal: its hypotheses, its facts, what its uses give, and its conclusion negated.

Use.description: A node read at a substitution where a guard holds: gives its conclusion there.

node.description: The node used (any, this one included).

subst.description: Its variables by terms of this node's frame (a variable a fact reads only where it is that fact's key).

premises.description: A tree per hypothesis of the node used, there.

descent.description: Its rank there is below this node's.

QMachine.description: A step machine over the rationals (Rationals.lean's Machine).

step.description: Values after a request (one left out keeps its value).

pre.description: Reads no input and no state.

Measure.description: A measure on a function's parameters: a tuple compared in order, each part Σ coef_i·size(param_i) + c.
